markdown_report:
The best next experiment is the prespecified **p=0.75 terminal-view allocation**, with checkpoint-linked accounting. At 20% progress, resolving implementation ambiguity is more useful than adding model complexity.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. First, masked-target discrimination is reasonably strong, but Electronics has weaker lower-tail margins. These training probes cannot establish validation HR@10. Second, item RankMe remains approximately 49–54 while user representations are more concentrated. This does not establish collapse or justify a geometry regularizer. Third, allocation snapshots describe fixed 64/64 branches while definitions describe Bernoulli allocation. Consequently, previous behavior cannot be attributed confidently to p=0.75.

Three literature insights guide the experiment. BERT4Rec already uses masked prediction and terminal masking [1]. The proposal therefore changes allocation rather than introducing a new objective. Sequence-shuffling studies motivate separating order from recency [2]. Sensitivity alone cannot establish current intent. Sampling research distinguishes task allocation from gradient interaction [3]. With separately normalized branch losses, 75% terminal examples does not imply 75% terminal objective weight.

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Controlled variable | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Allocation | Terminal-view probability | Realized counts, target denominators |
| Objective weighting | Branch coefficients | Applied coefficients, branch gradients |
| Context dependence | History perturbations | Paired frozen-model comparisons |

Three atomic ideas are candidates. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Audited p=0.75 allocation [1,3] | 2/6/3 | Simple, interpretable, useful foundation | Established technique; probability lacks measured optimality |
| Fixed 64/64 allocation with terminal loss coefficient 0.75 [1,3] | 2/5/2 | Directly changes objective emphasis | May weaken reconstruction; distinct from allocation |
| Recent-versus-older deletion diagnosis [2] | 3/6/4 | Tests context dependence without another predictor | Deletion also changes length and positions |

Select the first idea. Preserve each baseline branch’s context generator and replace fixed branch counts with 128 seeded Bernoulli draws per update. Retain separate branch target means and coefficients 0.5/0.5; record empty branches without redistributing weight. This changes allocation variance and target volume, not an explicitly prescribed terminal loss weight.

Logical steps: draw branches → construct unchanged branch-specific views → compute exact branch losses → update one BERT4Rec → persist measured accounting with the selected checkpoint. Generate diagnostic definitions from that saved configuration, and flag disagreements instead of repeating contradictory descriptions.

Preserve all four categories, seeds, training limits, diagnostic interfaces, and the pinned evaluator. Inference appends MASK and reads the maximum nonpadding index. Only host macro validation HR@10 can establish improvement; qualitative feedback motivates investigation but supplies no ownership, compatibility, or current-need labels.

idea.description: Evaluate one prespecified terminal-view allocation probability, p=0.75, in the corrected BERT4Rec baseline while preserving branch-specific contexts, separate target-mean losses, and coefficients 0.5/0.5. Persist measured allocation and configuration with each category’s single selected checkpoint, and derive diagnostic descriptions from those records.
idea.motivation: Supplied snapshots report fixed 64/64 allocation whereas metric definitions describe Bernoulli sampling, and another inspiration lacks allocation counters entirely. This prevents reliable attribution. A small allocation intervention with verifiable provenance fits early research progress and tests whether allocating more training views to appended-MASK prediction helps under the unchanged host metric. It does not directly infer unresolved needs or establish p=0.75 as optimal.
idea.implementation_notes: Apply this intervention to the host-supplied corrected baseline; the input does not contain enough backbone or host integration code to provide a faithful standalone train.py replacement. Keep 128 total generated views per update, drawing independent terminal indicators with probability 0.75. Preserve independent uniform eligible-user sampling conditional on branch, reconstruction on latest maxlen events with 0.15 MASK-only corruption and fallback, and the supplied terminal prefix-cutoff distribution. Preserve RNG stream separation and record the allocation stream explicitly; changing random draw consumption must be disclosed. Compute L=0.5*S_reconstruction/N_reconstruction + 0.5*S_terminal/N_terminal for nonempty branches, with zero contribution from absent branches and no weight redistribution. Preserve the catalog head, optimizer, positional convention, checkpoint selection, validation cadence and stopping behavior. Log realized branch examples, valid targets, detached CE sums, exact denominators, coefficients, objective contributions, and empty counts. Save cumulative and selected-epoch summaries with configuration/source identifiers; reload them for diagnosis. Generate definitions from saved protocol fields, validate counts against processed views and updates, and report contradictions explicitly. Do not infer branch identity from diagnostic terminal-position coverage. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch, and all ModelView interfaces. Loader tensors remain B x L. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs; 200 batches per epoch; single-GPU execution; and trial-local artifacts. Keep all compute within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Train and load exactly one model/checkpoint per category, without score fusion or checkpoint averaging. Preserve masked-target training without visible shifted-target leakage. Write a matching predictor using the reserved MASK, baseline positional IDs, history truncated to L-1 items, left padding, and maximum nonpadding readout. Keep twenty training-user full-catalog recommendations separate from pinned host validation. Use only supplied histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions; unavailable attributes and unsupported qualitative judgments remain unknown. Do not change splits, candidates, evaluator, or access test files, external data, pretrained weights, or other trials.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIG = {seed: 42, p_terminal: 0.75, batch_size: 128,
          branch_weights: {reconstruction: 0.5, terminal: 0.5}}

for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    baseline = host_corrected_bert4rec(category, CONFIG.seed)
    protocol = capture_actual_baseline_configuration(baseline)
    protocol.record_allocation_change('fixed 64/64 -> Bernoulli per generated view')
    counters = initialize_measured_counters()

    for epoch in unchanged_baseline_schedule(max_epochs=200):
        for step in range(200):
            branch_ids = seeded_allocation_rng(category, epoch, step).bernoulli(
                probability=0.75, size=128)
            # Preserve branch-conditional users, cutoffs, windows and corruption.
            batch = baseline.construct_branch_views(branch_ids)
            features = baseline.model.log2feats(batch.sequence)
            loss = differentiable_zero(features)
            for branch in [RECONSTRUCTION, TERMINAL]:
                S, N = baseline.catalog_ce_sum_and_valid_target_count(
                    features, batch.labels, branch_ids, branch)
                contribution = 0.5 * S / N if N > 0 else differentiable_zero(features)
                loss = loss + contribution
                counters.record(branch, S.detach(), N, contribution.detach())
            counters.record_realized_view_counts(branch_ids)
            baseline.optimizer_step(loss)
        summary = counters.snapshot(epoch)
        assert summary_matches_processed_views_and_updates(summary)
        baseline.select_checkpoint_with_unchanged_validation_rule(
            additional_payload={protocol, summary})

    save_one_selected_checkpoint(category)
    write_predictor_matching_selected_checkpoint(category)

predict(history, candidates):
    sequence = baseline_left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK])
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    j = maximum_index_where(sequence != PAD)
    return model.predict_score(features[j], candidates)

run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    metrics = existing_family_specific_probes(train_loader)
    metrics['training_branch_allocation'] = selected_checkpoint.summary
    definitions = definitions_from_saved_protocol(selected_checkpoint.protocol)
    report_protocol_counter_disagreements_explicitly(metrics, definitions)
    return {metrics, metric_definitions: definitions}

# Host independently evaluates fixed four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Checkpoint-linked accounting makes the allocation hypothesis interpretable and addresses a concrete contradiction in the supplied evidence.
originality.negative: Terminal masking and altered sampling probabilities are established techniques; this introduces no new modeling principle.

future_potential.positive: A verified allocation baseline supports later controlled studies of objective weighting, gradient variance, and context dependence within one network.
future_potential.negative: The chosen probability has no measured optimality justification and may leave qualitative relevance failures unresolved.

code_difficulty.positive: The core change is confined to training-view allocation and checkpoint metadata, with no backbone change.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful RNG handling, branch-context preservation, restored diagnostics, and consistency checks require careful integration with the unavailable baseline source.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional masked-item prediction for sequential recommendation.
Provides the masked prediction foundation and terminal prediction construction retained by this proposal.
limitations: Does not establish p=0.75 as optimal for this task.
Cannot resolve the local implementation’s allocation and diagnostic inconsistencies.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? An Analysis of Datasets for Evaluation of Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Investigates sequential structure through comparisons involving shuffled histories.
limitations: Shuffle sensitivity cannot establish current intent or causal preference evolution.
Its findings do not establish an improvement for the supplied four-category experiment.

related_work.title: PiKE: Adaptive Data Mixing for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Studies adaptive task sampling informed by gradient interactions.
Motivates distinguishing sampling allocation from objective coefficients and gradient behavior.
limitations: Reported pretraining behavior does not establish corresponding BERT4Rec branch behavior.
No supplied gradient measurements justify adaptive sampling or the selected probability here.
